findings.claim: CANONICAL: 'When the tool list is empty the verdict is `warn`, never `fail`, and ALL cases are `gap`. A `gap` says "no test covers this"; a `vulnerability` asserts the code would break, and that assertion requires reading the code.' and 'Before marking any case a `vulnerability`, verify the file exists and cite the exact path and line. A `fail` verdict requires a confirmed file path on disk.' and 'Never report a case against a file you have not seen.'
findings.checked: Compared the canonical fuzz-weaver GROUNDING RULES section word-for-word against the derived fuzz-weaver GROUNDING RULES section.
findings.found: The derived version deletes all three fuzz-weaver-specific rules above and replaces them with the generic 4-bullet block shared by review-ranger/mutant-hunter/spec-validator ('report warn, set the analysed/scanned count...', 'cite a real file path...', 'a count of zero inspected files with a non-empty findings list is a contradiction'). The generic block never states that every `case` must be forced to `gap` when tools are unavailable, and never gates a `vulnerability` classification specifically on a confirmed on-disk file path. This is exactly the failure mode the canonical text calls out by name ('This gate has previously invented vulnerabilities in files that did not exist') — the fix for that specific history was deleted.
findings.remedy: Restore the fuzz-weaver-specific rules verbatim: force all cases to `gap` (never `vulnerability`) when the tool list is empty, and require a confirmed on-disk path before any `vulnerability` classification.

findings.claim:
CANONICAL: '## When tool access is unavailable

  Emit exactly this shape, with counts reflecting that nothing was inspected:

  {"summary":{"filesAnalysed":0,"findingsCount":0,"blockerCount":0},"findings":[],"verdict":"warn"}

  NEVER emit `"verdict":"fail"` with filesAnalysed=0.'
findings.checked: Compared the full canonical perf-sentinel prompt section-by-section against the derived perf-sentinel prompt, looking specifically for the '## When tool access is unavailable' heading.
findings.found: The derived perf-sentinel prompt goes straight from '## Discover the codeline before you assess it' to '## GROUNDING RULES' — the entire '## When tool access is unavailable' section, including the mandatory exact-JSON output shape and the explicit 'NEVER emit fail with filesAnalysed=0' instruction, is missing. Only the generic GROUNDING RULES bullets remain, which state the same idea in prose but no longer pin down the exact required output contract.
findings.remedy: Re-add the '## When tool access is unavailable' section with the literal JSON shape and the explicit prohibition on emitting `fail` with filesAnalysed=0.

findings.claim: DERIVED: 'you scan the exported public surface under src/ (components, hooks in src/hooks, services, utils, interface types, Next.js API routes in src/api) ... Coverage gate: reconciliation must show >=80% of public API surface documented before proceeding to index build.'
findings.checked: Ran `find src/pages/api -iname '*.ts'` and `find src/api -maxdepth 1 -iname '*.ts'`, then read src/api/algolia.ts to see whether it is a Next.js route handler or a plain module.
findings.found: The real Next.js API routes (files Next.js's file-based router exposes as HTTP endpoints, e.g. src/pages/api/v1/autocomplete.ts, src/pages/api/v1/email-sign-up.ts, src/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts) live under src/pages/api/, not src/api/. src/api/ instead contains plain backend service/client modules (e.g. algolia.ts just exports an Algolia client and search params — no route handler) consumed by the real route files. Scanning src/api for 'Next.js API routes' misses the actual routing surface and misattributes an unrelated directory, which directly corrupts the totalExports/coveragePercent computation that gates the >=80% threshold.
findings.remedy: Point the API-routes portion of the scan at src/pages/api/ (route handlers), and describe src/api/ as backend service modules, not routes.

findings.claim: DERIVED: 'group documentation by this app's domains: ... and Next.js API routes (src/api)'
findings.checked: Same as doc-coordinator finding above: find src/pages/api vs src/api, and content of src/api/algolia.ts.
findings.found: Same mislocation — src/api holds service/client modules, not the file-based route handlers, which are under src/pages/api. This will cause api-doc-generator to label the wrong directory as the 'API routes' domain group and likely miss the actual route handlers, but since this only affects page grouping/labeling within generated reference docs (not a hard pass/fail gate), the impact is cosmetic rather than blocking.
findings.remedy: Group Next.js API routes from src/pages/api, and list src/api separately as internal service modules.

findings.claim: Derived ARTIFACT QUALITY BAR list: "HTTP 429 confirms an endpoint exists; HTTP 404 means the path does not exist on that host. Capture Retry-After, Content-Type, and X-* headers with curl -s -i."
findings.checked: Diffed the derived ARTIFACT QUALITY BAR bullet list against the canonical one line-by-line.
findings.found: Canonical includes an explicit fallback step between the 404 rule and the header-capture rule: "Try the host from API documentation first; if 404 is returned on all paths, try alternative host variants (e.g. …) — Capture response headers…". The derived brief drops this host-retry instruction entirely, going straight from the 404-exclusion rule to header capture. A spike-agent following only the derived text will, per its own retained rule ("HTTP 404 means the path does not exist on this host — exclude from endpoint list"), mark a vendor endpoint as nonexistent after one host fails 404 across the board, instead of trying alternate host variants (e.g. a sandbox vs. production subdomain for Stripe/Algolia/Contentstack) as canonical instructs. This narrows discovery thoroughness for exactly the kind of vendor-API probing this codeline's spike-agent brief calls out (Contentstack, Algolia, Stripe, Uniform).
findings.remedy: Restore the dropped instruction, e.g.: "Try the host from API documentation first; if 404 is returned on all paths, try alternative host variants (e.g. a sandbox/regional subdomain) before concluding the endpoint does not exist."
